title: WindSlayer-OutSpark Close Beta
era: Outspark EN closed beta, uploaded 2009-01-08 by Cytex, 640x480, 3:41. The HUD bottom-right button says 'Spark Shop'. Server 'Cecilia', channel 2. Snow falls in the early towns, so this is winter footage (a seasonal/event effect).
captions_notes: No captions. The description says: 'Just showing Close Beta and some towns. Fraps makes me laggy.' The whole video is a town tour with no combat.
summary: Town tour by the level 4 Novice 'Cytex' (blue spiky hair, pink/purple top). Order: Popola Village, Ozi Village, Monk Temple, Grand Master Smithy, Ozi Mountain area, Serien (City of Water) port, Atajokuna Settlement, Balderan Mining Village, with a brief pass through Shadow Cave. Shows the full EN beta HUD, the player right-click menu, the Player Info window, many NPC name tags with speech bubbles, EVENT NPCs, Premium Shop NPCs, the rotating [Announcement] tips, and live chat. No monsters are fought.

observations.what: Top-left status panel, dark navy with rounded frame. Orange labels 'HP' (red bar), 'MP' (blue bar), 'EXP' (yellow-green bar, about half full, spanning the panel width). Right of the HP/MP bars: an orange 'LV' label, a box with '4', and a box with 'Novice'. No portrait in this build.
Below the status panel is a quickslot bar with 8 empty slots numbered 1-8 in the corners, plus a page indicator '1' with a yellow down-arrow button on the right.

Top-right minimap window with a white title bar reading 'Cecilia(channel-2)' and a '-' minimize button. It shows a miniature of the whole map, with the map name in a white strip below ('Popola Village', later 'Ozi Village', 'Monk Temple', 'Grand Master Smithy', 'Serien, the City of ...', 'Atajokuna Settlement', 'Balderan Mining Vill...', 'Shadow Cave').
Bottom-right buttons: a large purple/magenta 'Spark Shop', then blue 'Avatar', 'PvP Etc' and 'Option'. Above them are small buttons: 'Msg' (greyed), 'Gift' (greyed) and a red-icon 'Report'.

Bottom-left, two lines. The upper line is a cyan system tip prefixed '[Announcement]' on a dark teal strip. The lower line is one visible chat line in white on black, with a '+' expand button at the far right. Chat seen: 'Topblast : ?' (0:00-0:36), 'Yeets : Looking for Party' (~0:48-1:00), 'Yeets : Were are the ssiyo?' (1:12-end). 'ssiyo' is the players' name for the beginner monster.

The [Announcement] tips rotate every few seconds in a fixed cycle. Texts read: 'When you reach level 30, you can do 2nd Class Change.' / 'Do not tell your personal information or password to others!' / 'GameMaster never asks your personal information or password!' / 'You can learn Herb Gathering from Rona when you reach level 3.' / 'Press Q to see all the quest list.' (0:26) / 'You can learn Mining from Gangdalf when you reach level 4.' / 'Open Stall can be learned from Leon when you reach level 6.' / 'You can learn Defense and Evasion from Gangdalf when you reach level 8.' / 'Reinforce can be learned from Leon when you reach level 7.' / 'You can get reputation points and Victy from Arena or Battle field.' (1:42) / 'You can change your class when you reach level 10.' (1:46) / 'You can buy Advanced Class License from Weapon Merchant at Ozi Village.' (3:32) / 'Strong Attack can be learned from Leon when you reach level 5.' / 'Concoction and Mineral Refining can be learned from Johabriner at town.'

Popola Village: snowy wooden/Asian-style village, snowflakes falling, snow on roofs and fences. NPCs stand in a row with dark name boxes (e.g. 'Go Rona', 'Gandwarf', 'Fyga Gangdalf'; spellings partly blurred). A white dog NPC is present. Several other characters are drawn as solid dark-grey silhouettes, apparently other players not yet loaded (guess, lag-related). NPCs show '!' bubbles.
Wooden signposts with arrows: 'Marble Mountain', 'POPOLA', 'Ozi Village Byroad 2', 'Marble Mt. Entrance'.
Player name tag: black rounded box with the name in white and a small red fist 'rank' icon on the left (the same icon as Rank 'Trainee' in Player Info). Another player 'Sniper' has the same icon.

NPC Nicolas, titled 'Self-styled Handsome', has an ambient white speech bubble: 'I'm scared to look at myself in the mirror.' At 2:44 he says: 'There's always the danger of falling in love with myself, ha ha!'

Ozi Village EVENT NPC: a green-haired girl in a purple witch hat on a red brick pedestal, under a pink arched 'EVENT' sign with wings and balloons. EVENT NPCs also appear in Serien (~1:56) and Atajokuna.
Signs: 'Serien The City of Water', 'Monk Temple'. NPC Dinnie 'Dualist Armor Merchant' (spelling uncertain) with the bubble 'Invest in reliable armor'.
The player jumps up a column of floating rock platforms at Monk Temple. A small dust puff shows on landing. Jumps are high, vertical platforming (MapleStory-like).

Monk Temple NPCs Gang-gun 'Monk Master' and Bruce 'Monk Instructor' (spellings uncertain) with ambient bubbles such as '...neglecting your training will...' and '...but I'll quickly brief you on them'. At 1:02 Bruce says: 'Flame Kick is a flying kick skill, and...' (a Monk skill name).

Grand Master Smithy interior (a 'WEAPON' sign, weapon racks, a shield with crossed swords). A shopkeeper NPC in a leopard-print helmet speaks in bubbles: 'Equip the weapon that suits your level.' / 'Feel free to browse through my weapons, and see if you like any.' Bubbles are white rectangles with dark-red/black text and hyphenated word wrap ('s-uits', 'th-rough').

Right-clicking another player opens a dark-navy vertical menu titled with their name 'Kuzenko' and an X close button. Items in order: 'Char. Info', 'Trade', 'Make Party', 'Whisper', 'Add as Friend', 'Converse', 'Copy Name', 'Praise', 'Report'.

'Player Info.' window (gold title, X close button). Fields: Name 'Kuzenko', 'Lv.5'; Class 'Novice'; Guild 'N/A'; STR 13, INT 2, DEX 4, SPR 6; Rank 'Trainee' with the red fist icon; Manner 0. A 3x3 empty grid sits at the top right. Below is a 2x8 equipment row showing a white shirt, a wooden stick weapon, blue pants and blue shoes (the starter gear).
Blue-white crystalline sparkle particles burst at player feet. Guess: a winter-event or teleport/arrival effect; the cause is not visible.

Ozi outskirts: a Fortune Teller NPC ('You'd want to go to Shadow Guild hall.'), a 'Farm' stone, a cow, and signs 'Wild Cliff' and 'Ozi Mountain' (snowy stone pillars). At about 1:16-1:20 orange flame-like sparks appear, possibly a portal or map transition (guess). The next scene is Serien.

Serien (City of Water) port: wooden docks, life buoys, sea, a ship. Signs 'Entrance to Serien', 'Serien Port 2', 'Scuba Gate', 'Sky Gate', 'Seren Meadows'. The 'Premium Shop' building sign is blue/pink, even though the HUD button says 'Spark Shop'.

Serien NPC name tags are two-line black boxes (name, then role) in pale text: 'Shaori / Grocer', 'Mikomakisho / Bank Keeper' (bank NPC exists), 'Frenaiga / Friend List Helper' ('Hello, I'm here to help you make new friends.' / 'If you want to add friends on your Friend List...'), 'Luxary / Shop Assistant' at the Premium Shop ('...purchase useful items for your adventures!'), and 'Johabriner / Crafting Master' ('...equipment or exclusive consumable items?').
Angel statue in town, probably a save/revive point (guess). A small pink blob creature follows a pink-haired player, possibly a pet (guess).

Atajokuna Settlement: savanna scenery, a flat-topped mountain, a ship. Signs: 'Seren Wilderness', 'Guild Hall', 'Flea Market', 'Atajokuna Gate', 'Katapaha Territory', 'Balderan Mine'. 'Herbal' and 'Farm' stones, a Premium Shop, Johabriner (Crafting Master), and an EVENT NPC. One NPC bubble reads: 'Well, I can't disclose that info, hahaha!'

Balderan Mining Village: an autumn/golden palette, stone walls, barns, mine carts, CAUTION crates. Buildings 'POTION SHOP' and 'WEAPON SHOP' (a boar-like NPC: '...you're interested? Couldn't hurt to try.'). A miner NPC says '...minerals as you learn more and more about them.' Signs: 'Balderan Mine Slope', 'Mining Settlement Entrance', 'Upper Tunnel', 'Red Rock Mt Gate', 'Shadow Guildhall'. A bank keeper and a Premium Shop NPC ('Click on me, and move to the Premium Shop!', so the shop NPC teleports you). Erin: 'Nice to meet you, I'm Erin.' / 'Sigh; I wonder when my big brother will come back home.'
The minimap briefly reads 'Shadow Cave' (a mine/cave map adjacent to Balderan).
No combat, damage numbers or monsters appear. The only creatures are town animals (dog, cow) and NPCs.

title: Wind Slayer Gameplay Footage
era: Outspark EN, uploaded 2009-02-06 by MMOHuts. Low resolution (320x240). The HUD bottom-right reads 'Premium Shop' instead of the 'Spark Shop' in the Jan 2009 video, so this is a different/newer build. Minimap title 'Cecilia(channel-1)' (the channel digit is blurry).
captions_notes: Auto-captions only contain '[Music]'/'Heat'/'Woohoo' (background music, no commentary).
summary: About 2.5 minutes of a Monk ('silvercloud', teal hair, red outfit, female) grinding monkey monsters on 'Village Byway'. The map has tall stone cliffs, floating rock platforms, sunflowers, a waterfall, a stone arch bridge and tiled roofs below. It shows the EN combat presentation: green damage numbers dealt, red numbers taken, large orange starburst hit effects with orange comic hit-lettering, a white dizzy/stun-like icon over monsters, and mobs clustering on the player. HP falls over time. The same [Announce] tip rotation as video 1. Ends on the Option button tooltip.

observations.what: Same HUD layout as video 1: HP (red), MP (blue) and EXP (green, mostly empty) bars at top-left. Level/class text reads like 'LV 1? Monk' (blurry; Monk is the class after the level-10 change). The quickslot bar below is full of skill/item icons (a fire orb, a white glove/fist, a brown scroll, a blue item, dumplings/buns, a red potion).

The minimap window (white title 'Cecilia(channel-?)') shows 'Village Byway' in its strip. Bottom-right buttons: purple 'Premium Shop', blue 'Avatar', 'PvP Etc', 'Option', with small 'Msg', 'Gift'/'cert' and red 'Report' buttons above.
Hovering 'Option' shows a black tooltip: 'System Settings: Optimize your keyboard settings, and set macro and system options.'

Cyan tip line with the prefix '(Announce)' (vs '[Announcement]' in video 1; low-res read). Tips in order: 'Press Q to see all the quest list.' (0:00) / 'Strong Attack can be learned from Leon when you reach level 5.' (~0:18, 2:13-2:22) / 'Open Stall can be learned from Leon when you reach level 6.' (~0:24) / 'Defense and Evasion ... Gangdalf ... level 8' / 'Concoction and Mineral Refining can be learned from Johabriner at town.' (~0:52-0:58) / 'Reinforce ... level 7' / 'You can buy Advanced Class License from Weapon Merchant at Ozi Village.' (~1:03) / 'You can get reputation points and Victy from Arena or Battle field.' (~1:12) / 'When you reach level 30, you can do 2nd Class Change.' (~1:31-1:36) / 'Do not tell your personal information or password to others!' (~1:37-1:45, 2:33) / 'GameMaster never asks ... password' / 'You can learn Herb Gathering from Rona when you reach level 3.' (~1:54).

Map 'Village Byway': large stone-block cliff walls with diagonal grassy slopes, floating rock islands, sunflowers, green trees, a waterfall column, a stone arch bridge (0:39-0:40, 2:07-2:09), Asian-style tiled roofs at the bottom, blue sky with cartoon clouds, and a volcano-like peak in the background. A wooden 'Cliff Slope' sign with a left arrow at 0:22-0:31 and 2:31-2:34. No snow.
A red/orange ring orb with a dark center appears next to the player (also at 0:36 above the player's head). Likely a skill/buff visual; not identified (guess).

Monsters seen: 'Monkey Soldier' (brown monkey wearing a round blue/red/yellow striped hat like a Chinese general's cap), 'Monkey Sergeant' (hatless brown monkey), and 'Monkey Farmer' (possibly 'Monkey Tamer'; blurry), a bigger brown ape near the tree at 1:30-2:04. Name tags are black rounded boxes with light text, under the monster's feet. No level boxes or HP bars are visible on monster tags.

Monkeys stand on several platform tiers. When the player engages, they gather around the player (4-6 overlapping at once at 0:52-0:58 and 1:12-1:30 under the tree), apparently chasing and attacking in melee (guess: aggressive or at least retaliating). They walk and hop between tiers.

Big hit effect: an orange/red explosive starburst with a white-hot center, roughly 1.5x the character's size, on the monster. Spiky orange comic-style lettering pops above it (an onomatopoeia hit word; text unreadable at 320x240). It lasts about 0.2-0.3 s.
Other hits show smaller orange splash lettering over monsters ('POW'-style, unreadable). A large pale-yellow burst engulfs the player at 0:12 (probably a skill).

Damage dealt appears as large green digits with a dark outline above the monster (e.g. '32', '36', '38', '42', '43', '47', '50', '14', '16', '20', '35'). Damage taken appears as smaller red digits with a dark outline near/above the player (e.g. '2', '3', '4'). Numbers float up and fade in about 0.5-1 s. Several numbers can be on screen at once during mob fights.

10fps sequence. At 2:14.6 a translucent blue/purple ghost-like figure appears behind the player (skill aura, guess). At 2:14.7 an orange starburst plus hit word on the Monkey Soldier. From 2:14.9 a white round spiral/skull icon floats over the monster's head for 2+ s, with a small orange text box next to it (likely a stun/dizzy status marker, guess). At 2:16.2 the player attacks again, and at 2:16.5 a green '42' (dealt) and a red '2' (taken) appear.
The player sprite leaves a long horizontal trail of afterimages while dashing/attacking through a group (a dash or multi-hit skill, guess).

No items are visibly dropped on the ground and no EXP/gold text is visible. Kills are hard to confirm at this resolution; monkeys vanish from the cluster over time. HP goes from about 100% to about 60% (~1:40) to about 45% (~2:30). No level-up is seen.
A large yellow round smiley emote appears above the player's head (emotion/emoticon system).
Another player (blonde) with a name tag joins the area, so the field is shared multiplayer.
Player name tag: black box, white name 'silvercloud', a small icon on the left (the rank icon).

title: Wind Slayer Gameplay Video HD
era: KOREAN client, not Outspark, even though it was uploaded 2009-01-23 by FREEMMO (640x480, 1:46). All UI is in Korean; the logo is gold 'WIND SLAYER' with a sword and blue '윈드슬레이어'. Guess: the Korean commercial service before the EN launch (a 2006-2008 KR build). Its HUD layout differs from both EN videos.
captions_notes: No captions available.
summary: Full new-player flow on the KR client: logo, server/channel select, 'waiting for server' popup, CHARACTER screen, character creation (name, 5 appearance selectors, 4 stats with +/- and bonus points), entering the tutorial map '모험의시작' with a key-guide overlay, the elder NPC tutorial quest (gives a stick weapon, asks you to kill one monster, explains attack/pickup keys and 'I' for inventory), equipping from inventory, walking right via a signpost to '초보용사냥터' (beginner hunting ground) through a loading screen, fighting orange sack/pumpkin blob monsters, dying (the player turns into a stone statue) and the 'revive in town' popup.

observations.what: White splash screen with the WindSlayer logo (gold 'WIND SLAYER', sword, blue Korean text).

Server/channel select over a sky-and-cloud background. A light window with a dark-navy title bar holds 10 channel buttons in 2 columns x 5 rows. Each button has a name on the left and a gauge (population bar) on the right; the text is unreadable. Two blue buttons at bottom right (likely 확인/취소, OK/Cancel). The cursor is a white gauntlet/hand.
Modal popup '서버의 응답을 기다립니다.' ('Waiting for the server's response.') after picking a channel, and again after pressing start. Then a fade to dark.

'CHARACTER' header (light-blue outline text) at top-left. The background is a town plaza with a knight statue fountain. Four blue buttons at right: '캐릭터 만들기' (Create), '캐릭터 삭제' (Delete), '게임 시작' (Start game), '나가기' (Exit). A copyright line sits at the bottom (unreadable). The created character stands on the grass at left with a name tag.

'캐릭터만들기' window. '이름' (Name) text field; the character preview in a grey box. 5 appearance rows, each with ◀ ▶ arrows: the first is hidden by the cursor (likely 머리/hair), then 얼굴 (face), 상의 (top), 하의 (bottom), 신발 (shoes). Clicking cycles hair and outfit colours (pink/blue/orange/red tops). Male, spiky blond hair shown.

Stat block with 4 stats, each with a value box and green '+' / '-' buttons: 힘 (STR), 지혜 (wisdom/INT), 민첩 (agility/DEX), 건강 (health; likely the SPR/VIT equivalent). Below is a '남은보너스'-style field (remaining bonus points). The player clicks + on 힘 (STR) at 0:40-0:43 and the bonus field changes, so starting stats are hand-allocated from a bonus pool. Buttons '만들기' (Create) and '취소' (Cancel). Compare EN Player Info: STR/INT/DEX/SPR.
New character 'Kukabara' appears in the character list, standing on the grass.

KR HUD. Top-left: a small portrait box, a red HP bar, a blue MP bar, a level box '1' and class text '초보여행자' ('Beginner Traveler' = Novice), with a green EXP bar across the top. Top-middle: quickslot bar with slots numbered 1-8 and a page button. Top-right: minimap window titled with the map name ('모험의시작' = 'Start of Adventure'). Bottom-right: a row of about 12 small square icon buttons (including a red X), not the EN text buttons. Bottom-left: chat line.

First-login translucent key-guide overlay. Arrow keys labeled 점프 (jump, up), 왼쪽/오른쪽 (left/right), and 내려가기/사다리이동 (go down/ladder, down). A 아이템줍기 (item pickup) label over one letter key and 약한공격 (weak attack) under another letter key (the letters are blurry). A long SPACE key labeled roughly '대화/창열기' (talk/open window; guess).

Quest markers: an orange '!' bubble over NPCs with a quest available (a female NPC and the elder). After accepting, the elder shows a green '?' bubble (1:14, in progress). While in dialog the player has a white '....' speech bubble.

Elder NPC dialog (old man with glasses and a helmet). A large portrait bleeds off the left edge; a gold title in quotes (village elder '...'); body text in a white panel; a next arrow. Page 1 (1:03): '넓은 세상으로 모험을... 맨손으로... 허허허~' (going adventuring bare-handed?). Page 2 (1:06): '내가 여기 간단한 무기를 줄테니 우선 마을 앞마당의 몬스터를 한마리만 사냥하고 오게나 ... 어디 한 번 해 보겠나?' ('I'll give you a simple weapon; first go hunt just one monster in the village's front yard. Will you try?'), with accept/decline buttons. Page 3 (1:07): '몬스터를 공격하려면 " ? " 버튼을 누르고 몬스터가 떨어뜨린 아이템을 줍고 싶을 때는 " ? " 버튼을 누르면 된다네~ 그 전에 " I " 버튼으로 아이템창을 열고 내가 준 무기를 착용하는 것을 잊지말게나~' ('press ? to attack; press ? to pick up items monsters dropped; first open the inventory with I and equip the weapon I gave you'), with a 확인 (OK) button. This confirms monsters drop items on the ground and pickup is a manual key.

Inventory: 4 vertical category tabs on the left (the first, orange, is selected), an item grid, and 2 fields at the bottom (probably money). The weapon is a wooden stick/branch. Tooltip: item name (roughly '굵은나뭇가지', 'thick branch', guess), 분류 무기 (type: weapon), two stat lines, a description, 요구레벨 1 (required level 1), 요구직업 초보여행자 (required class Novice), 요구성별 남녀공용 (unisex), a red line, and 판매가격 (sell price).

Tutorial map '모험의시작': green grass, sunflowers, a white dog NPC with an info-sign bubble, and a wooden signpost '초보용사냥터 →' (beginner hunting ground). The player walks off the right edge to change maps, with no portal object visible.

Map transition: fade out, then a white loading screen. A card shows the logo and a red-haired girl with goggles, with the speech bubble '...니아에 오신것을 환영합니다.' ('Welcome to ...nia'; the continent name is cut off) and a blue progress bar.

Map '초보용사냥터' has tiered grass platforms and sunflowers. The monster is an orange sack/pumpkin-like blob with a small leaf sprout and an angry face (matches the EN beginner mob 'Ssiyo'/Pupu type, guess). Its name tag is a dark box with magenta/purple text. The player's name tag is a grey/dark box with white text. Other players are hunting the same map.

White/cyan swing arcs on attacks. Small damage digits: red '1' and green '2' (same scheme as EN: green dealt, red taken; guess by analogy). When hit, the player sprite flashes as a solid black silhouette for a frame or two. Small grey square item icons float or lie in the field (likely dropped items, guess).
Death sequence: a gold ring of bubbles/stars and a dizzy blue face, then the player becomes a grey stone statue on a small pedestal (the corpse representation). The monster stays next to the statue.

Death popup: '체력이 다해서 쓰러졌습니다. 클릭하시면 마을에서 부활합니다.' ('Your HP ran out and you collapsed. Click to revive in town.') with a blue button '부활합니다' ('Revive'). Death means click to respawn in town, with no in-place revive shown.
Bottom-left chat shows the player's own lines in white, in the format 'Kukabara : ...'.
Outro: WindSlayer logo screen.

title: Wind Slayer Tutorial Video (MMOHuts, uploaded 2009-02-06, 1:43, 640x480, MMOHut watermark bottom-left)
era: Outspark English client, early 2009 (open-beta era). Evidence: 'Spark Shop' button, 'WSP' currency line in the Bag, 'Spark Items' bag tab, minimap server title spelled 'Cecilia(channel-1)', and the upload date. The HUD matches the 2008/2009 EN layout.
captions_notes: No captions obtained: the English auto-subs request returned HTTP 429, and the video's description has no mechanics text. Everything below comes from frames only. Timestamps are accurate to about 0.5 s. The full-white or washed-out frames at 0:25, 0:49, 1:17 and 1:28.5 look like editing transitions, not game effects (guess).
summary: About 100 s of a brand-new Novice girl named 'Remotay' (teal hair, orange top, white skirt). She takes the Elder's first quest, 'Elder's Test', from Murubisiri, gets a Wooden Stick, walks through a sparkling portal into Novice Hunting Park, and punches then clubs 'Ssiyo' mobs. The quest completes after the first kill. Each kill logs +10 EXP, and she reaches LV 2 at about 1:29. The video shows the 2009 EN HUD (HP/MP/EXP panel, 8-slot quickbar, minimap, announce ticker, Msg/Gift/Report, and the Spark Shop/Avatar/PvP Etc/Option buttons). It also shows the Equipment and Bag windows, the Wooden Stick tooltip, the comic hit words (CHUD/KRAKK), green damage numbers, loot left lying on the ground, and a blue 'LEVEL UP!' text with a 'Level up' button that appears next to the chat box.

observations.what: Top-left panel: rows labelled HP (red bar), MP (blue bar) and EXP (grey track, green fill), with 'LV 1' and 'Novice' to the right. Below it is a quickslot bar with slots 1-8 plus a page number '1' and a yellow down-arrow. No numeric HP/MP values are shown on the HUD.

Top-right minimap box. Title bar reads 'Cecilia(channel-1)' with a minimize button, then a map thumbnail with dots, and a footer with the map name ('The Beginning of the...' in the start village, later 'Novice Hunting Park').

Bottom strip: an '[Announce]' ticker in cyan text, the chat input line showing the player name 'Remotay', a '+' button, small buttons 'Msg', 'Gift' and 'Report' (red icon) above the right side, and big buttons 'Spark Shop' (purple/pink), 'Avatar', 'PvP Etc' and 'Option' (blue).
Translucent key-help overlay in the start village: Jump [Up], Move Left [<-], Move Right [->], Move Down & Portal [Down], Item Pickup [W], Basic Attack [S], [SPACE] Use NPC & Object.

NPC 'Murubisiri' has a two-line green name tag 'Murubisiri' / 'Elder of the Village': an old man with a blue cap, round glasses, mustache and satchel. A '!' speech bubble above him means a quest is available. Another player, 'krows' (black hair, overalls), is nearby.
Player name tag is a dark rounded box with a small fist icon (class icon, guess: Novice) followed by the white name. Other players ('krows', 'Kalin') use the same style.

Dialog window: orange title 'Elder of the village  Murubisiri', large portrait on the left. Text: 'You must master the adventuring basics before you go off exploring wherever you please. I mean, you don't even have a weapon yet. You'd better be well armed if you don't want to be killed by the monsters out there. Hahaha!' A blue quest list below shows 'Elder's Test'.

Second page: 'I can provide you with a simple weapon if you use it to hunt down a monster in the Novice Hunting Park. That will prove that you're ready to go adventuring. You ready to try my little challenge?' Buttons: Accept / Decline.
After Accept, the Elder's bubble changes from '!' to a green '?' (quest in progress). A white speech bubble 'Help me~' appears above the player (player chat or emote bubble).
Bottom-right system log in small white text: 'You've received Wooden Stick. (Count:1)'. The quest-start item goes straight to the bag.

At the village edge, a sign 'Novice Hunting Park ->' stands next to a white dog NPC and a cyan-sparkle portal on the ground. Tip box: 'To enter next area, press Down arrow key after locating yourself on the sparkling portal.'
About 1 s fade to black, then the new map appears. There is no separate loading screen.
Map 'Novice Hunting Park': tiered grassy cliffs, floating grass platforms, waterfall background, sunflowers. Sign 'Small Town <-' at the left entrance.

First mob 'Ssiyo': a round brown/orange furry ball with big eyes, some with a curly sprout on top. Its name tag is a grey-blue box reading 'Ssiyo', with no level shown. Many Ssiyo wander the platforms. When the player targets or hits one, its tag turns purple/blue-highlighted (guess).

Before equipping a weapon the player punches bare-handed. Each hit shows a green damage number '1' above the mob and a comic hit word in red/orange ('CHUD', 'KRAKK'), sometimes with a small orange starburst label.
A small red '1' floats near the player or at the top of the mob stack. Guess: damage taken by the player, since the player HP bar is visibly reduced at about 1:28.

Equipment window: title 'Equipment', sections 'Weapon & Shield', 'Armor & decoration' (orange shirt, white skirt and shoes equipped), 'Accessories', 'Pet', a 'Detail' button and a bottom bar showing '0%'. Both weapon slots are empty.
A large round rainbow/white orb with a yellow core flashes near mobs on the right. It appears again at 1:16 and near another player at 1:31. Guess: a mob spawn/respawn or skill effect.
A killed Ssiyo shows X-eyes (dizzy face) and then fades out. There is no ragdoll or knockback beyond a small flinch.

title: WindSlayer 2 - Tutorial, Class Change, and Class Special. (Part 1) (TamerKoh, uploaded 2012-03-31, 10:18)
era: WindSlayer 2 English relaunch client, 2011-2012. Evidence: minimap server title 'Sesilia(channel-1)', 'Premium Shop' with iCash/Mileage, tip 'Visit us on facebook.com/WindSlayer2', a new cinematic tutorial, Character Select with '2nd PSW' security and a PvP rank table. Despite the title, this Part 1 ends at Lv 5 Novice: no class change is shown.
captions_notes: There are no English captions for this video. The description says only 'Just a quick run through.' Everything comes from frames. Contact sheets were made at 1 frame per 5 s, with 0.25-2 s bursts around key moments.
summary: Starts at Character Select (5 characters, 12-slot cap) and plays the WS2 story tutorial. Scripted dialogues with a village elder and a blonde girl teach movement, SPACE interact, [S] weak attack, dash, double-jump (Up twice) and 'V' to open the bag. The player fights Nupoco, Footear Rabbit and Cheeky Mupoco, opens chests with a cast bar, and gets a Ruby. The video then enters Nubeae Town with the full WS2 HUD and browses the Premium Shop. Quests seen: 'Open Secret' (Lv 2 plus 500 Gold and potions), 'Limping Adventurer' and 'Adventurer's Token'. Hunting covers Tokki (Lv.01), Pokang (Lv.02) and Angry Tokki (Lv.04). Combat shows a target frame, combo counter, the Good/CRITICAL!/BAD grade words, comic hit words, coloured damage numbers and gold-coin drops. The video also shows the stat-bonus system, an NPC weapon shop in Popola Smithy, and item tooltips with prices.

observations.what: 'Character Select' screen: title in a cyan banner at top-left, a '2nd PSW Warning!' button at top-right. Tip: '[Login Security Feature] Activate [authorization number] at the top. You can protect your account by verifying your second password...' Info panel: 'IHerdULiekPurple Lv.1 / Novice' and a Rank / Fluctuation Chart table (Total, Class, Arena) all reading 'PVP not yet played.' Buttons: Create / Delete / Select / Back. Notice: '[Notice] You can create up to 12 characters!' Scripted story at a tree-house village with a giant purple flower. An old man (miner hat, goggles, glasses) talks to a blonde girl (the tutorial protagonist portrait, not the player's pink-haired avatar). Lines include 'Maybe you should reconsider. You're too young...', 'If you want to stop me, you'll have to lock me up in a binding stone...', 'Very well. I won't stop you if you can prove to me that you're ready for this journey.', 'I've left an old chest in a small cave that is in the mountain behind the village.' Big portraits sit left and right, and the text box has a red speaker name. No standard HUD is visible during the tutorial (as far as the sampled frames show).

Key-prompt boxes with the format '<key> <action> / Press the key.': '[->] Move right', '[SPACE] Operate & Open', '[SPACE] Pick up item', '[S] Weak Attack', '[->][->] Dash', and 'Double Jump - Press [up] key twice.' Jump is the Up arrow. A bottom banner reads 'Press Space Bar to proceed to the next conversation'.

Opening a treasure chest shows a '....' bubble over the player and an orange cast/progress bar 'Opening the chest;;'. Chests have green name tags ('Wood Box', 'Wood Box1'). The log then shows 'You've received Health Po(tion)...'

Hint: 'Press 'V' on your keyboard to open your storage box. Right-click on the energy potion to boost your energ...'. Later: '...Right-click on the thick tree branch to hold it.' Right-clicking equips or uses an item. The Bag window has tabs Equip./Consum./Misc./iCash, a 6-column grid, and a gold field reading 0.

Character information window at Lv.1: 'IHerdULiekPurple Lv.1', class 'Novice', title 'N/A', tabs Basic Info./Extra Info. Four primary stats: STR 4 and 2/2/2 for the others, with INT among them. Attack 3-9, defense 3, 'Bonus 0', HP 154/154, MP 110/110, and four elemental-resist fields at 0. Lower tabs Equipment / Premium / Pet show the paper doll.
Tutorial mob 'Nupoco': an orange fox-like critter. Mob name tags are black rounded boxes with cyan text and turn red when the mob is hit or aggroed. The first hits show the 'THUD' hit word.

Blue/purple crystal cave with a stone floor and yellow chevron signs. An NPC in a bunny hood ('HA HA HA! Catch me if you can!', 'I brought company this time!') brings mobs 'Footear Rabbit' (white rabbit with a club) and 'Cheeky Mupoco' (orange critter). The player fights them, and the combo counter appears on the right.

The cave chest gives the Ruby: log 'You've received Ruby.' Back in the village the elder says the red gem 'seems to have mystical powers'. Then a large cyan centre banner reads 'The portal to the next area has opened'.
Wooden 'Nubeae Town' sign. NPC 'Nubeae town girl / Dami' has a two-line green tag and ambient speech bubbles ('Take care of yourself.', 'Don't give up!'). Red/pink arrow markers point at quest NPCs.

PREMIUM SHOP: tabs New Items / Featured / Fashion / Appearance / Consumables / Pet / Functional / Package / Wish-list, with sub-tabs Face/Hairstyle/Dye/Skin. Item cards have a NEW badge and Buy/Gift/Wish buttons. Examples: Ulie Pet Cube 100 Cash, GuriGuri Pet Cube 100, Ghastly Skin 299, Purrrfect Couple Set [F]/[M] 1,199, Purrrfect Shirt/Pants [F] 28 days 399, face items at 349 each, Trendy Hairstyle Cube 499, other hairstyles 599. The right pane has a character preview, Purchase All / Default / Del, Purchased Items, and a Bag with 'Add Bag Slot' / 'Add Bank Slot'. Footer: iCash 457, Mileage 0, 'Charging iCash', 'Check iCash Balance', EXIT. Confirm box: 'Trendy Hairstyle Cube (M) 499 iCash / No Option / 28 days / Total 499 iCash / [ ] Buy it with mileage / Purchase these cash items?' OK/Cancel.

WS2 HUD. Top-left box 'Lv. [n] <name>' with a pink HP bar and blue MP bar, no numbers. Top-right minimap titled 'Sesilia(channel-1)' with a map-name bar ('Nubeae Town'); coloured dots show players/NPCs (red and green figures). Below it is a collapsible 'Quest Log (0/5)'. Bottom: a chat log with tabs General / Friends / Guild / Party / System / +, an 'EXP' label with a green EXP bar across the bottom, and a two-row quickslot (1-8 and Q W E R T Y U I) with page '1' and a down-arrow. Buttons: 'Char', 'Arena', 'System', and a pink 'Premium Shop'.

Green system lines in chat: 'Class Advancements are available at Lv. 10, Lv. 30 and Lv. 60.', 'The use of 3rd party software is a violation of the ToS. Accounts will be suspended accordingly.', 'To toggle windowed and full screen mode, press ALT+ENTER.', 'Visit us on facebook.com/WindSlayer2 for updates, events and more!'

Big-portrait NPC dialog 'SOMUNNE, the village gossiper' (tag 'Nubeae town man / Somunne'), with a Yes/No prompt then OK. The Quest Log shows '(1/5) [Open Secret] Please go to Ojirapi'. The centre green message '[Open Secret] You are ready to complete the quest.' appears on reaching the target. Turn-in NPC is 'OZIRAFI, the nosy village lady' (tag 'Nubeae town woman / Ojirapi'). NPC bubbles: '!' = quest available, '?' = turn-in, '....!' = new.

Quest completion log: 'You've received (+45) experience points.', 'You've received 500 Gold.', 'You've received Health Potion(S). (Count:10)', 'You've received Mana Potion(S). (Count:10)', '[Open Secret] Quest Completed.' A lavender 'Level up!' tutorial popup follows: 'Congratulations! You have reached level 2! ... you'll also receive a bonus that can improve the basic skill of your choice. You can open the Character Info window, and distribute bonuses...' It includes a picture of the stat window with an 'Auto stat' button.

Stat growth per level: Lv2 Bonus 4 (+ buttons beside each stat, plus an 'Auto stat' button), attack 4-9, MP 112. Lv3: STR 8, attack 4-10, HP 158/158, MP 114/114. Lv4: STR 14, attack 5-12, HP 160, MP 116. Lv5: STR 20, attack 9-15, HP 162, MP 118. So a Novice gets +2 HP and +2 MP per level, and the stat bonus is spent in STR here. INT tooltip: '<INT> Enhances Mage and Priest attrib.. increase MP.'

Map 'Novice Hunting Park(Tar...' (the name carries a Target Lv suffix). Target frame at top centre: mob portrait, cyan name 'Tokki', 'Lv.01' on the right, and a red HP bar that shrinks with hits. The portrait is replaced by a red prohibition symbol when the mob dies. When hit, a mob's tag turns red and a small HP bar appears under it.

Grade words above the player: green 'Good', orange/yellow gradient 'CRITICAL!', orange 'BAD'. Comic hit words: KRAKK, CHUD, THUD. Damage numbers are 1-5 in several colours (green, pink, cyan-blue; orange on crit). Mobs flinch when hit; on death the mob turns into a dark silhouette and fades, and its tag goes black.
Combo counter at bottom right: large digits plus 'Combo!'. Green up to at least 19; orange from 22 up (22, 26, 28, 29 and 32 seen). It keeps counting across several mobs.

Kills log '(+18)', '(+14)' or '(+12) experience points' for Tokki. Gold drops as spinning gold 'G' coins that scatter and bounce around the kill spot, then vanish as the log shows 'You've received 21 Gold.' Whether pickup is automatic or by key is unclear. Item drops lie on the ground (e.g. an orange crystal), and logs read 'You've received Mystery Cube Pieces. (Count:1)', 'Grinding Stone 100. (Count:1)', 'Crude Club. (Count:1)'.

Level up in combat: big yellow 'LEVEL UP' text and a golden light pillar on the player. A small 'LEVEL UP!' icon appears next to the HUD name box. From Lv5 a purple 'SKILL UP+' icon shows above the chat area (skill point available).

Walking past the 'Low cliff ->' sign: a sparkle on the player, then a short fade to black. Map 'Low Cliff' has a rope bridge and NPC 'Grazie' ('GRAZIE, the limping traveler'), who gives '[Limping Adventurer] Please go to Nertikamale'.

(Count:10)', 'Mana Potion(S). (Count:10)', 'Crude Club. (Count:1)' and '[Limping Adventurer] Quest Completed.' in green, which also shows as a centre banner.
'Popola Hill 1(Target Lv...)': 'Pokang' (Lv.02) are orange cat/dog-like mobs that crowd the player. Another player, 'Dalina' (blue hair), hunts nearby.

Crude Club tooltip: 'Weapon / Not Tradable / Physical Damage +3 / Required level: 3 / Required class: Novice / Required gender: All Genders / Price: 287Gold / Resell Price: 56 Gold / A crude club made with a thick branch.' The Bag shows 1150 gold.

'Popola Village' NPCs with two-line green tags: 'Aspiring Artist / Rona', 'Event Mania / Nicolas', 'Village Boy / Leon', 'Grocer / Shaomei' (SUNDRIES stall), a PREMIUM stall NPC, and 'Popola village girl / Heartweak'. Signs: 'Popola Hill 1 <-', 'Well ->', 'Forest Path 1 ->', 'Popola Courtyard'. Another player 'PenguimVoltZ' is present. Entering a door gives a sparkle and a short fade.

'Popola Smithy' interior: NPC 'Popola Armor Merchant / Porederman', dialog titled 'Merchant specializing in equipments'. The 'Shop' window has a Category dropdown, tabs Equip/Helmet/Top Armor/Bottom Armor/Gloves/Shoes, a 9-column grid and a Buy button; items the player can't use are tinted red. title: WindSlayer 2 - Tutorial, Class Change, and Class Special.  (Part 2)
era: WindSlayer 2 relaunch (English, 2012; uploaded 2012-03-31). The HUD advertises facebook.com/WindSlayer2, the server/channel is shown as 'Sesilia(channel-1)', and the menu buttons are Char/Arena/System/Premium Shop. This is not the 2008/2009 Outspark client.
captions_notes: YouTube auto-captions exist but contain only [Music]/[Applause] tags, so there is no spoken commentary. The video description is just 'Just a quick run through.' All text below was read from the screen. Timestamps are contact-sheet labels (±3 s).
summary: Silent 10-minute playthrough of the WS2 English beginner flow. A Novice (IHerdULiekPurple) goes from Lv4 to Lv11. The run covers Popola Courtyard/Popola Village/Old Well/Popola Hill quests (Angry Tokki, Stomachache Frog, Pokang), learning the Common skills, the Lv10 'Choose a Class' popup, and a trip through Ozi Village and the Occupational Area ('Job Field' gate) to Mage Town, where the class change to Mage resets stats. It then learns Ice Bolt/Fire Bolt, picks up the 'Arena Hopeful' title from the Arena NPCs, and fights Ape Soldiers (Lv09) in Wild Cliff. It is a good reference for the WS2 HUD, the quest text format, loot and exp messages, hit words, grade words, the combo counter and level-up visuals.

observations.what: Top-left: a box with 'Lv. N' and the character name, a red HP bar and a blue MP bar (e.g. 'Lv. 9 IHerdULiekPurple'). Top-centre: a target frame with the monster's face portrait, its name in blue text, 'Lv.04'/'Lv.09', and a red HP bar on a black track. Top-right: a minimap window titled 'Sesilia(channel-1)' with the map name (e.g. 'Popola Courtyard 1(Targ...'), monsters as red icons and the player as a green icon. Below it is a 'Quest Log (N/5)' panel listing tracked quests and objectives. Bottom: a thin green EXP bar across the full width labelled 'EXP'; chat tabs 'General | Friends | Guild | Party | System | +'; a 2-row quickslot bar (keys 1-8 and Q W E R T Y U I, page number '1' with arrows); big 'Char', 'Arena' and 'System' buttons; a pink 'Premium Shop' button. Small icons above the quickslots: mail envelope, 'SKILL UP+', 'NEW QUEST', a yellow '!'.

Rotating green tips in the bottom-left chat: 'Class Advancements are available at Lv. 10, Lv. 30 and Lv. 60.' / 'Visit us on facebook.com/WindSlayer2 for updates, events and more!' / 'The use of 3rd party software is a violation of the ToS. Accounts will be suspended accordingly.' / 'To toggle windowed and full screen mode, press ALT+ENTER.'
Comic onomatopoeia pops out on each hit in orange/red-yellow outlined letters: 'THUD', 'CHUD', 'KRAK' (sometimes 'KRAKK'). They appear next to the monster being hit.

Damage numbers are small digits with a white/cyan-blue outline (e.g. '6', '7', '15', '30', '13', '5') that float up from the monster. At low level they are small (1-30). No separate critical colour was clearly seen in this video.

A 'BAD' grade word in orange/yellow block letters appears above the player and monster during Ape Soldier fights. A green 'Good' is seen in the companion video. The grade words appear next to the hit words.

A large green italic 'N Combo!' counter sits in the lower-right of the play field, above the chat (e.g. '4 Combo!', '11 Combo!', '15 Combo!', '2 Combo!', '8 Combo!'). The number increments per hit and resets after a pause.

Monster name tags are a small black box with white text under the mob (e.g. 'Angry Tokki', 'Pokang', 'Ape Soldier'). A monster that is engaged or damaged gets a RED-background name tag and a small HP bar (green fill, red) directly above the tag. Idle mobs keep black tags.
Killed monsters turn into a dark/black silhouette and fade out where they stood. Some are knocked slightly back while flinching.

Loot drops ON THE GROUND at the kill spot: gold coins (round gold coin with a 'G') and item icons such as a brown leather piece or small dark round seeds/bombs. The player walks over them to pick them up. Pickup messages scroll in the lower-right message log: 'You've received Golden Leaf. (Count:1)', 'You've received 28 Gold.', 'You've received (+37) experience points.' / '(+22) experience points.' / '(+25) experience points.'

A black popup box above the target shows kill progress, stacking the older counts below: 'Kill Pokang (1/5)' up to '(5/5)', 'Kill Ape Soldier (1/5)' ... '(4/5)'. Collect quests show e.g. 'Golden Leaf (4/5)' and 'Herb Seed (1/3)'. When done, green centred text reads '[Adventurer's Token] You are ready to complete the quest.' and later '[Elder's Test] Quest Completed.'

On level up, a tall golden light pillar with 'LEVEL UP' text rises over the character. A persistent yellow 'LEVEL UP!' badge with arrows then sits beside the top-left HP/MP box for several seconds. Levels seen: Lv6 (0:40), Lv7 (1:05), Lv8 (2:00), Lv9 (4:20), Lv10 (5:25), Lv11 (8:55).

'Character information' window: name plus 'Lv.N'; class box ('Novice') and a second box 'N/A'. Tabs 'Basic Info.' and 'Extra Info.' (tooltip 'Battles Tab'). Stats are STR, INT, VIT and DEX with '+' buttons (tooltip 'Increase STR'), attack range (e.g. 12-22, 13-24, 16-33, 17-34), magic attack, defense (3, 17, 19), a 'Bonus' point count and an 'Auto stat.' button, HP/MP bars with numbers (Lv6: HP 164/164, MP 120/120; Lv8: HP 168/168; Lv9: HP 165/170), and fire/ice/etc. elemental resist boxes. Lower tabs 'Equipment | Premium | Pet' with a paper-doll. Novice stats: Lv6 STR 24/INT 2/VIT 2/DEX 2, Lv8 STR 29, Lv9 STR 35 with bonus 1. So points are manual, about 5 per level, and this player put them in STR.
The 'Bag' window has tabs 'Equip | Consum. | Misc. | iCash', a grid of slots, and gold shown at the bottom (2255, then 4055, then 10860).

Light Leather Gloves: 'Gloves / Not Tradable / Defense +1 / Required level: 6 / Required class: All classes / Required gender: All Genders / Price: 490Gold / Resell Price: 98 Gold / Gloves made of cheap, thin leather that only offer minimal protection.' Wooden Sword: 'Weapon / Not Tradable / Physical Damage +6 / Required level 1 / Required class: Novice / Required gender: All Genders / Price: 602Gold(?) / Resell Price: 119 Gold(?) / A wooden sword.' Title item 'Arena Hopeful': 'Not Tradable (red) / Required level: 1 / Required class: All classes / Required gender: All Genders / Price: ??? / Resell Price: 0 Gold / The rising star of the Arena!'

The 'Skill' window has tabs 'Common' and 'Vocational'. Each row has an icon, the name, 'Lv.N / Passive' or 'Active' (or 'Not Learned Yet'), and a 'MASTER' (green) or 'LEARN' (grey/orange) button. Common skills: Dash Lv.1/Passive MASTER, Double Jump Lv.1/Passive MASTER, Powerful Attack Lv.1/Passive MASTER, Private Shop, Craft, Add Attribute (partly hidden), Collect Lv.2/Passive, Enhance Equipment, Levitate, Wisdom Lv.1/Passive. Mage (Vocational) skills: Ice Bolt Lv.1/Active, Fire Bolt Lv.1/Active, Wind Bolt, plus more rows not readable. Learn messages: 'You've learned skill (Craft).', '(Collect)', '(Wisdom)', '(Ice Bolt)'. The learned skills were dragged into quickslots 1-3 (Ice Bolt, Fire Bolt, Wind Bolt).

Craft: 'Skill level: 2 / 20, Required level: 7, Required class: All classes, [Next Skill Level: 3] Required level: 10, Make an item with the right ingredients'. Private Shop: 'Not Learned Yet / Required class: All classes / [Next Skill Level: 1] Required Level: 6 / Open a shop where you can sell your personal items. / Condition : Talk to Popola Village grocer at level 9'. It was learned by 9:00 ('Skill level: 1/1'). Enhance Equipment: 'Required class: All classes / [Next Skill Level: 1] Required level: 20 / Bring out the best of an equipment by tweaking its abilities. / Condition: Talk to Johabrinner(?) at level 20'. Wind Bolt: 'Required class: Mage / [Next Skill Level: 1] Required level: 10 / MP -8 / Wind attack +20 / Cast a sharp attack that splits space / Learn : Magician Skill Master'.

At Lv10 a purple popup 'Level 10! Choose a Class' appears: 'Congratulations! You have reached level 10! You can change your class for the first time. Changing your class for the first time means you can choose to be a warrior, mage, monk, rogue, archer, or priest.' It shows a tree with Novice at the top and 6 portraits below: Warrior, Rogue, Archer, Monk, Mage, Priest. Footer: 'Please see the Help Page for detailed methods to change your class.'

The class change happens by talking to 'Mage Master Estarose' in Mage Town. A popup reads 'Congratulations! Mage is your new class.' [OK], and the green text reads '[Way of Mage] Quest Completed.' The reward text mentions Gold ('You've received 3000 Gold', partly legible) plus potions. Afterwards the Character information shows class 'Mage' with ALL stats reset to 0 and 'Bonus 46' plus the 'Auto stat.' button. HP went to 184/184 and MP to 96/305, then 111/541 and 128/609 as INT was added. So the first class change refunds every stat point for re-allocation. Tooltip on INT: 'Enhances Mage and Priest attribute Attack Power and increase MP'. Tooltip on VIT: 'Increase VIT'.

The dialog box has a large NPC portrait on the left, the NPC name in blue bold plus a subtitle, typewriter text, and OK or Yes/No buttons. NPCs seen: 'LEON, who wants to be an adventurer' (tag 'Village Boy Leon'); 'GANGDALF, village chief of Popola' (tag 'Popola Village Chief Gangdalf'; line: 'I know someone at the Ozi Village, and I will write you a recommendation. Take that with you and go to the Fortune Teller Grandma at the Ozi Village.'); 'MEI, the fortune teller' ('Welcome to Ozi Village. Ah, this is not your first time? ... Did you forget who I am? Hohoho!'); 'ESTABLUE, the magic teacher' / 'Mage Instructor Establue'; 'NAMET, the PvP title manager' / 'Arena Title Manager Namet'; 'Arena Keeper Yuppo'; 'Mage Master Estarose'; 'Grocer Shaori' (SUNDRIES shop, bubble 'Welcome to my shop!'); 'Aspiring Artist Rona'; 'Event Maria' / 'Event Nicolas' (guess); 'Popola village girl Heartweak' ('Oh dear! You scared me!'); 'Playground Keeper Nori'; 'Friend List Helper Friendaiga'; 'Region Movement Guide' (a big purple bird by a red POST box); 'Warehouse Keeper' (name unclear). Talking to an NPC gives a small menu bubble with 'Quest' / 'Shop' options, and NPCs show '...' speech bubbles and random chat bubbles.

Quest names seen: [Adventurer's Token] (Golden Leaf 5), [Dry well] (Key 1/1), [Guardian Tree], [Village Elder Gangdalf], [Elder's Test] (Pokang Kill 0/5), [Faded Photo], [Gangdalf's Secret], [Herb Tea Materials] (Herb Seed 3/3, 'Please go to Rona'), [Gangdalf's Letter 1], [Let's open a Personal Store] ('Please go to Shaori'), [Letter from fortune teller], [Fortune Results] ('Please go to Maulsallam'), [Fortune teller Grandma] (Pork 0/3, Peach Seed 0/3), [Fortune Telling Tools] (1/1), [Way of Mage], [Arena's Rising Star], [Let's Learn Levitate]. The Quest Log cap is 5 ('Quest Log (4/5)'). Quest-available NPCs show '!' and '?' bubbles.

Ozi Village has an Arena area with 'Arena Keeper Yuppo' and 'Arena Title Manager Namet' (bubble 'Why must this Helmet be so big?! Grrr..!'). Completing [Arena's Rising Star] gives the title 'Arena Hopeful'. It then shows in green with a sprout icon above the player's head from 8:05 on. No arena match is shown.

Map names (minimap titles): 'Popola Courtyard 1(Target Lv...)', 'Popola Village', 'Old Well Inside', 'Popola Hill 1(Target Lv...)', 'Ozi Village', 'Occupational Area', 'Mage Town', 'Wild Cliff(Target Lv.8~...)'. Signposts: 'Popola Courtyard', 'Forest Path 1', 'Dried Well', 'Popola Hill 1', 'Ozi Village', 'Popola', 'Mage Tower', 'Ozi Village' (arrow). Ozi Village has an East-Asian style with a giant golden Buddha statue, a 'Flea Market' building, the 'SUNDRIES' shop and a 'PREMIUM SHOP' building. The Occupational Area has a winged 'Job Field' arch gate that leads to class towns; 'Warrior School' and 'The Rockslin' (archer?) signs were seen. Mage Town has grey stone cliffs and blue floating light orbs.

Map changes fade to a black screen with a small spinning circle (loading indicator) in the upper-middle, then fade in. There is no loading artwork. Players enter portals by walking to signposts/arches, with a golden sparkle effect at the portal.

title: WindSlayer 2 first-impressions gameplay (MMOHut, commentary by 'Omni')
era: WindSlayer 2 relaunch by Ignited Games (commercial launch late Nov 2011), Hamelin-developed. Later than our 2008 EN client. Title logo reads 'WIND SLAYER 2'. captions_notes: Auto-captions were read in full. Mechanics the commentator describes: 'WindSlayer 2' is really WindSlayer 1 with updates. Outspark shut down the old service and characters did not transfer. Only world 'Cecilia' (Sesilia) with one channel. Everyone starts as a class-less Novice, with class advancements at Lv 10, 30 and 60 ('five or six' classes, each branching into two). Leveling is much faster than in WS1 (a claim of level 30 in about a day). Arrow keys move and double-tapping a direction dashes. Double jump is available. The attack keys were found under System > Keyboard settings: S is the basic attack and D a stronger attack. Space bar loots and advances dialogue. Pressing Down twice (or Up) at a portal changes map. There is an Auto-stat button. The commentator guesses stat resets happen at Lv 10. The game has PvP and crafting. Money is called 'Gz/G coins'. He calls monster names 'Poopoo' (WS1) versus 'Pokang' (WS2) and thinks some monster and map names changed. He mentions duping and hacking problems at launch.
